import os,glob,re,json
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))

def f(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    out=[r[:] for r in g]
    seen=set()
    for i in range(h):
        for j in range(w):
            v=g[i][j]
            if (i,j) in seen: continue
            # check if this starts a main-diagonal run (>1 same value down-right)
            ii,jj=i+1,j+1
            while ii<h and jj<w and g[ii][jj]==v: ii+=1;jj+=1
            if (ii-i)>1:
                for k in range(i+1,ii): out[k][k-(i)] if False else None
                for k in range(i+1,ii): pass
                for k in range(i+1,ii):
                    out[i+k][j+k]=v
                    seen.add((i+k,j+k))
            seen.add((i,j))
    return out

print(f(G['Demo pair 1 input'])==G['Demo pair 1 output'])
res=f(G['Test input'])
print(json.dumps(res))

import os,re,json
from collections import Counter
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
gi,go=G['Demo pair 2 input'],G['Demo pair 2 output']
for i in range(len(gi)):
    a=''.join(str(x) if x!=Counter(y for r in gi for y in r).most_common(1)[0][0] else '.' for x in gi[i])
    b=''.join('#' if go[i][j]!=gi[i][j] else '.' for j in range(len(gi[i])))
    print(a,b)

And down-right from (10,13)? The added 3s below: (11,12),(12,11),(13,10) — that's down-LEFT from (10,13), continuing the anti-diagonal d=23. So the run is {(9,14),(10,13)} on anti-d=23, extended down-left. But up-right from (9,14) blocked by 4 at (8,15)? No wait, direction along anti-diagonal: up-right would be (8,15) which is 4 — blocked ✓. Down-left continues to edge.

And 3 main diagonal {(7,13),(8,14)}: up-left extends; down-right from (8,14) → (9,15) is 0, blocked ✓.

So the run is defined over BOTH diagonal directions?? The shape {(7,13),(8,14),(9,14),(10,13)}: (9,14)-(8,14) vertical... Actually this looks like two diagonal runs meeting at a vertex, like a "V". Both runs extended in their own direction until blocked/edge. That matches demo 1 too: 5s at (15,1),(16,0) are on anti d=16, one cell each side of... they're adjacent diagonally (down-left). Run {(15,1),(16,0)} anti; extend both ends: up-right from (15,1) free to edge! But output did NOT add those. Hmm, but maybe extension stops when hitting another color's LINE? Or when extension would exit grid through... (15,1)→(14,2) free all the way to top-right corner region. Why not extended?

Hmm wait — maybe rule: extend only in the direction where you can go ≥ some length? Or extension stops when about to hit the other object? The 1-run extended down-right away from the 5s. The 5s' up-right extension goes into empty area though. Maybe rule: extend each maximal same-color diagonal run in BOTH directions, but stop at non-bg, AND additionally the whole figure must be consistent... Demo1: 5 run extended up-right would make a long ray; the given answer lacks it. Contradiction with my earlier verified hypothesis.

Alternative interpretation: maybe the rule isn't per-color-run but per-line: each colored cell lies on a full diagonal line; the line is drawn complete through ALL its cells of the same color, filling bg between/around them, stopping at any non-bg. In demo1, line d=16 for color 5 contains cells (15,1),(16,0) plus beyond all bg → should fill (14,2)... not filled. Still contradiction.

Unless blocking applies to ANY color: does the 1-ray cross the 5 line? 5 anti d=16 vs 1 main d=15 — parallel, no crossing. Hmm.

Maybe direction chosen = the direction pointing AWAY from the object's centroid/bbox? 5-run centroid (15.5, 0.5); extending up-right increases i decreasing j... vector away from origin? 1-run extended down-right (increasing both) — away from top-left origin. 5 run extended? None. What if rule: each run extends ONLY in the direction where i+j (or distance) increases overall / where the run points "forward" based on some majority orientation of the shape? D1 shape cells sorted: 9@(15,0), then 5s at rows15-16 cols0-1, then 1s going down-right. The whole thing is an arrow pointing down-right; rays follow arrow: the 5 is the "body", the 1 extends the arrow tip. Only the tip extends? But demo2 3s extend both branches... unless the 3 branches are part of the same arrow.

Demo3: 8 extends up-left; 3 extends both ways; 2 extends down-right. Three rays. Demo4: 6 extends up-left; 1 extends down-left; 4 extends down-right. Two rays per pair, opposite-ish.

Hypothesis: pairs of objects form arrows where two colors form the wings and third color is the shaft? Demo1: 5 (top-left body) + 1 (shaft extending down-right) → draw the full arrow: shaft extends fully; wings just mark direction. Arrow: direction down-right determined by 1-run; 5 marks nothing extra. Result: only 1 ray. Demo2: 4 ray up-right from apex; 3 forms big V — both arms extended. The 0 single cell blocks the 3 arm. Demo4: 6 extends up-left, 1 down-left, 4 down-right.

Maybe simpler: treat each color's cells as forming a polyline; extend each END segment in its diagonal direction until blocked by non-bg or grid edge. D1: segments: 9 single (no extension), 5 cells {(15,1),(16,0)} diag adjacent → endpoint (16,0) direction (-1,+1)? segment slope -1: extend from both endpoints: (15,1)+(-1,+1)=(14,2) free — but output has none! Still contradicted. UNLESS extension requires the path not to eventually touch another color's extension? They don't touch.

Hmm wait — maybe I misread demo1 output row 14-2? Let me recheck: earlier diff showed expected kept 6 there. Yes.

OK here's another thought: maybe the transformation draws rays such that the TOTAL result is symmetric-ish / complete lines: perhaps each PAIR of same-direction neighboring same-color... 

New idea: rays extend until length equals number of cells of that color + something? D1 1: 2 cells → 7 added (total 9). D2 3: 4 cells → 10 added (total 14). D4 6: 2 cells → 6 added (8 total). Lengths vary by object size.

Alternatively maybe the correct reading: the input shapes are incomplete lines (like dashed lines?) and we need to complete EACH maximal straight line (any slope ±1) to full grid extent... but only within regions not containing other colors? D1 5 anti-d=16: cells (15,1),(16,0) — completing gives nothing more except up-right extension. Not present. Unless completing means drawing between the two cells (they're adjacent, nothing to do). Then why extend 1s? Because 1 cells (16,1),(17,2): not adjacent along their line (d=15): gap between (16,1) and (17,2) is adjacent diagonally actually. Also completed. Ugh.

What distinguishes 1-run from 5-run in D1? 5's run, extended, would reach the TOP-RIGHT edge region; 1's extended reaches bottom-right. The existing 9 is at (15,0) top-left. Maybe rule: extension goes toward the farthest edge? Both could claim.

Or maybe: extension happens from the end FARTHER from the shape's anchor? In D1, what's the "anchor"? Perhaps the multi-cell structure: {5,5,1,1} forms a small chevron/arrow. The open end points down-right → extend along that opening. Chevon arms: 5-arm goes up-left, 1-arm goes down-right. Opening is down-right. Extend down-right only. D3: 3-arm open both ways? 3 cells (3,8),(4,7),(5,6),(6,5) — full anti line; extended both ways to edges. 8 arm {(3,5),(4,6)}: open up-left → extended. 2 {(5,7),(6,8)} open down-right → extended. D1: 5 arm {(15,1),(16,0)} anti; open end (15,1) goes up-right. Yet NOT extended. Difference: in D3 the 8 arm was extended despite being short and far from anything. In D1 the 5 arm open up-right is NOT extended.

Difference between D1's 5 and D3's 8: position relative to other colors? D1 5 arm sits directly ABOVE the 1 arm; together they'd form a ">" shape; extending 5 up-right breaks the symmetry toward making separate rays. D3 all three arms extended because they naturally radiate.

Alternative framing: the figure is an arrow/chevrons; output completes each line to the EDGE BUT only the lines whose extension direction is NOT pointed at / blocked by... D1 5-line up-right extension would pass near (14,2)...(2,14)? and 1-line extends (18,3)..(24,9). Do these two rays intersect? 5 line: i+j=16; 1 line: i-j=15. Intersection: i+j=16,i-j=15 → i=15.5,j=0.5 — no.

Distance from original shape? 5 extension starts right next to shape. 1 extension also next to shape. Hmm both equally close.

What if the rule involves counting: extend the ray longer in the direction with MORE room available? D1: 5 up-right room 14 cells; down-left 0 (blocked by OOB essentially at (16,0)→(17,-1)... actually down-left from (16,0) is immediate off-grid). So choose max room: 5 extends up-right — contradicts again!!

Grr. Unless... wait, maybe I have the direction wrong: maybe the 5 extension should go up-LEFT? No, the diagonal through (15,1),(16,0) is anti (slope -1): moving up-left means i decreases, j decreases: (14,0)? that's not on the line. Line direction: Δ(1,-1). Extending from (15,1): (14,2),(13,3)... up-RIGHT. Yes.

Let me re-examine D1 input once more: row15: "95..........." col0=9,col1=5. Row16: "51.......": col0=5,col1=1. Row17: "..1......": col2=1. So 5s at (15,1),(16,0); 1s at (16,1),(17,2). Note (16,0) and (16,1) horizontal neighbors. Interesting! Maybe runs include horizontal adjacency too, and the "line" is determined by the longest chain? Chains: 9 isolated. 5-chain via (15,1)→(16,0) diagonal; 1-chain (16,1)→(17,2) diagonal. Also note 9 at (15,0) adjacent to both 5s.

Output adds 1s: (18,3)..(24,9). That's continuing the 1 diagonal. Nothing else. In D2, output extended both 3 arms and the 4 arm. In D2, are the 4 cells connected to the 3 cells? 4 cells (7,16),(8,15); 3 cell (7,13),(8,14),(9,14),(10,13). (8,15)-(8,14) horizontal neighbors! And (9,14)-(10,13) diagonal, (7,13)-(8,14) diagonal. So the 3-object is a zigzag, attached to the 4-object horizontally. Output extends everything outward away from the junction? 4-object junction at (8,15); its other end (7,16) extends up-right away. 3-object junction near (8,14)/(9,14)... its top branch (7,13) extends up-left away from junction; bottom branch (10,13) extends down-left away. 0 at (9,15) blocks 3 from extending down... no wait 0 sits between (9,14) and (9,15)... (9,15) is adjacent to (8,15)=4. 0 blocked the downward extension of... 3's down-left branch already extended. 0 itself stays.

D1: 5-object junction at (16,0)/? 5 cells (15,1),(16,0); 1 cells (16,1),(17,2). Junction: 5 at (16,0) adjacent to 1 at (16,1) horizontally? and 9 at (15,0). Which side is the "open end" of each object? 5: the diagonal run {(15,1),(16,0)} — open end (15,1) points up-right. NOT extended. 1: run {(16,1),(17,2)} open end (17,2) points down-right — EXTENDED.

Both ends point away from the junction region ((16,0)-(16,1) horizontal pair, plus 9 above-left). 5's open end (15,1): up-right direction. Extended? No! 1's: yes. What differs?! 

Unless... the extension must point AWAY from the junction measured as the OPENING: maybe the extension direction is chosen so that the ray points away from the NEAREST OTHER COLOR? 5's open end nearest other color: 1 at (16,1) — distance from (15,1) to (16,1) = 1 (directly below!). So 5's ray would point... away from 1 → up-right. Still no extension.

Hmm, or maybe extension goes in the direction where the ray length BEFORE hitting another color's ray is maximized... 

Let me count cells: 1 gets 7 new cells (rows 18-24, cols 3-9). Grid height 25. The 1 ray spans rows 16..24, cols 1..9 — reaches bottom row (row 24 = last row!) and col 9. The 5 potential ray (15,1)..(2,14)? reaches col 14 = last col but row 2 ≠ last. Maybe rule: extend toward the corner/edge you'll HIT FIRST that is farther? Or extend until you reach a grid EDGE, choosing whichever edge — and preferring the edge that... D1: 5 ray hits right edge; 1 ray hits bottom edge. Maybe prefer... hmm in D2: 4 ray hits right edge (0,23): row 0 = top edge too! hits corner. 3 upper branch hits top edge. 3 lower branch hits bottom/left? (13,10): continues (14,9),(15,8)... would hit left edge at (18,5)? w=24, h=14: from (13,10) down-left: (14,9),(15,8),(16,7),(17,6) then (18,5) OOB. Hits bottom edge at row 17. Wait h=14: rows 0..13! (13,10) IS the last row. So 3 lower branch stops AT the edge. And upper branch at (0,6) hits top edge. So both 3 branches hit edges. 4 branch hits top/right corner. 0 stays single.

So D2: EVERYTHING extended to edge. D1: 1 ray hits bottom edge; 5 potential ray hits right edge at row ~2 — NOT extended. Why???

Wait — maybe check: does the 5 potential ray actually hit the right edge before the bottom? From (15,1) along (−1,+1): cells (14,2),(13,3),(12,4),(11,5),(10,6),(9,7),(8,8),(7,9),(6,10),(5,11),(4,12),(3,13),(2,14),(1,15) — out since w=15, cols 0..14, so (1,15) invalid; stops at (2,14). Reaches right edge at row 2, not bottom. Fine.

Maybe the rule: extend toward the FARTHER edge? For 5: right-edge distance vs bottom-edge distance: current (15,1): distance to bottom = 9; to right = min col-to-14 = 13. Choose the nearer? 1's ray from (17,2): down to bottom: 7; right: 12. Nearer = bottom → extend ✓ (it did). 5: nearer = right (dist 13 vs 9)... it extends to right anyway by proximity, yet doesn't happen ✗. Farther: 5's farther = bottom (9 < 13? no, bottom dist 9, right 13, farther = right) — extend to right ✗. Neither works consistently!

Honestly maybe the real rule: extension direction = away from the MULTI-COLOR REGION center. Let me compute centroid of all non-bg cells in D1: cells (15,0),(15,1),(16,0),(16,1),(17,2). Centroid (15.8, 0.8). 5-end (15,1): away vector = normalize away from centroid: dir from centroid: (−0.8, 0.2); projection onto line dirs (-1,1) and (1,-1): dot1=-1*0.8+1*0.2=-0.6<0 → away direction is −(−1,1)=(1,−1) i.e. down-left → off-grid immediately → no extension ✓!! 1-end (17,2): from centroid (1.2,1.2); projections: onto (-1,1): -1.2+1.2=0; tie. Onto line dir (1,-1): 1.2 >0 → continue (17,2)→(18,3) ✓. Tie broken how? Maybe by which side faces more space... (18,3) fine.

Check D2: junction-ish. All cells: 3:(7,13),(8,14),(9,14),(10,13); 4:(7,16),(8,15); 0:(9,15). Centroid ≈ ((42)/16? rows: 7+8+9+10+7+8+9=58, /7=8.28; cols:13+14+14+13+16+15+15=90, /7=12.86). Top branch endpoint (7,13): away vector ≈ (-1.28,-0.86); proj onto (-1,1): 1.28-0.86=0.42>0 → extend up-left ✓ (output has it). Bottom branch (10,13): vector (1.72,0.14); proj (1,-1): 1.68>0 → down-left ✓. 4-end (7,16): vector (-1.28,3.14); proj (-1,1): 1.28+3.14>0 → up-right ✓. Also (8,15): vector (-0.28,2.14) → up-right ✓ same ray. 0: single cell, no extension (need run len≥2? or singles stay). 

D1 5: computed gives NO extension ✓. D3: 8 endpoint (3,5): cells 8:(3,5),(4,6); 3:(3,8),(4,7),(5,6),(6,5); 2:(5,7),(6,8). Centroid rows: 3+4+3+4+5+6+5+6=36/8=4.5; cols: 5+6+8+7+6+5+7+8=52/8=6.5. 8-end (3,5): vector (-1.5,-1.5); line dirs (-1,1),(1,-1): proj = -1.5+1.5=0 → tie! Hmm. Output extends up-left (i.e. (-1,1)). With tie, which way? Tie-break needed. Maybe use the perpendicular component sign against... Alternatively tie-break by more space? Up-left space from (3,5): to top edge rows 0-2: 3; right edge cols 6-14: 10. More space = right/down... but output chose up-left (less space)! Alternatively tie-break: direction where ray first exits... both exit eventually. Hmm.

Tie-break candidate: extend away from the rest of the figure using the 2nd-order term, or pick direction minimizing distance to the bounding box? Or maybe: among tied, choose the direction pointing away from the grid CENTER? Center (h/2,w/2)≈(6.5,6.5). Up-left from (3,5) moves further from center? From (3,5) to center: (3.5,1.5); up-left step (-1,1) changes distance² by -(1)^2+(1)^2=0 — neutral too! Since line passes through center-parallel... the direction is exactly parallel to vector from figure centroid to global center? weird.

Alternative tie-break: the extension should avoid... let me just also check 3-endpoints in D3: (3,8): vector (-1.5,1.5); proj onto (-1,1): 1.5-1.5=0 tie too! But output extended up-right from (3,8) to (2,9),(1,10),(0,11). And down-left from (6,5): vector (1.5,-1.5); proj (1,-1): 1.5+1.5=3>0 → down-left ✓. So 3 has ties at top endpoints too.

So many ties. Maybe the tie-break: choose direction pointing away from grid centroid (h/2,w/2)? Global grid center: D3: (6.5,6.5). At (3,8): step (-1,1) → new cell (2,9): dist to center squared: (4.5)^2+(2.5)^2=20.5 vs staying... stepping up-left: (Δdr,Δdc)=(-1,1): dist change = -2*3.5*(-1)? distance squared f=(r-6.5)^2+(c-6.5)^2; at (3,8): (3.5)^2+(1.5)^2=12.25+2.25=14.5. Step (-1,1): (4.5)^2+(2.5)^2=20.5 — INCREASES → away ✓. Step (1,-1): (2.5)^2+(5.5)^2=6.25+30.25=36.5 — increases more! So away-from-global-center picks (1,-1) i.e. down-left ✗. Opposite of desired. Towards center picks up... at (3,8): toward center = up-left? dr from center: 3-6.5=-3.5 → move +1 (down) reduces |dr|; dc=8-6.5=1.5 → move -1 (left). Toward = (1,-1) down-left ✗. Desired (−1,+1). Hmm.

Tie-break: maybe prefer the direction with FEWER cells before exiting (shorter ray)? At (3,8): up-right exits after 3 steps (to (0,11)); down-left exits after 5 steps ((4,7)... wait down-left occupied by 3's own cells! (4,7),(5,6) are 3. Continue: (6,5),(7,4),(8,3),(9,2),(10,1),(11,0) — 6 more steps, then edge (all bg). Total 6. Fewer = up-right ✓!
At (3,5) for 8: up-left 3 steps to edge; down-right: (5,7) is 2, blocked! 0 steps. Fewer = 0 → no extension ✗ (but output DOES extend 8 up-left). ✗.

Hmm. At (3,5) down-right is blocked by 2 at (5,7) — so effectively extension length 0; up-left gives 3. Rule "extend toward the side with more room" worked for (3,5) but failed (3,8) (where up-right room 3 < down-left 6). Conflict.

Unless... for (3,8), extension along down-left collides with the 8-line? 8's line is main diag d=-2 passing through (4,6),(3,5),(5,7). s=11 line through (3,8): does it hit d=-2? intersection (r,s): r+s=11,r-r'=... d=-2: r-c=-2, c=r+2 → r+r+2=11 → r=4.5,c=6.5 — not integer. So lines are interleaved offset by 0.5; no collision.

OK different approach: maybe the rule concerns WHICH color extends: maybe only ONE color per "object cluster" extends — the color whose run touches the "outside"? All do.

Alternatively maybe the intended rule is much simpler: the figure consists of several straight line SEGMENTS arranged radially (like spokes of a wheel/arrow tips). Each spoke has a line of a single color; the output EXTENDS EACH SPEAK'S LINE OUTWARD to complete a full star pattern, where spokes point AWAY from a common center. Common center might be approximated by the shape centroid. Spokes: D3 center ~ (4.5,6.5). 8-line direction away from center: vector from center to (3.5,1.5)... 8 cells lie on line r-c=-2, perpendicular normal (1,1); direction away = sign of (center_on_line - ...). For line L, pick orientation such that spoke points away from cluster centroid: unit perp = ±(1,1)/√2; choose sign s.t. s·(centroid - p) < 0... at p=(3,5): centroid-(p)=(1.5,1.5); s=(1,1)·(1.5,1.5)>0 → choose s=(-1,-1) i.e. direction (-1,1)?? perp vectors are (1,1) and (-1,-1) for main diag direction of motion? Careful: motion along main diagonal: deltas (1,1) or (-1,-1). Dot with (1.5,1.5): positive → choose (-1,-1) = up-left ✓!!
Recheck (3,8) on anti diag: motion deltas (1,-1) or (-1,1). centroid-p = (-1.5,1.5). Dot (1,-1): -1.5-1.5=-3<0 → choose (-1,1) = up-right ✓!! 
D1 (15,1) 5-run: line anti d=16, motions (-1,1),(1,-1). p=(15,1), centroid(15.8,0.8): vec=(0.8,-0.8). Dot (1,-1): 0.8+0.8=1.6>0 → choose (-1,1)=up-right → EXTEND ✗!!! Still fails. Argh.

Ugh, D1 kills it again. Unless centroid should be computed only from... including 9? 9 at (15,0): centroid = (sum rows 15+15+16+16+17=79 /5=15.8; cols 0+1+0+1+2=4/5=0.8). Same as before (9 contributes 0 to col sum). Same result: up-right predicted, reality none.

D1 is really anomalous under almost every rule. Unless... wait, maybe I should double-check the test expectation differently: maybe the answer for the test case is simply the input unchanged, and D1's anomaly (5 unextended) coincidentally matches "unchanged". And in demos, extensions happen when... maybe when the line would EXIT THROUGH AN EDGE OPPOSITE the start? 5-line exits right; 1-line exits bottom. D3 8 exits top-left; 3 exits both... 2 exits bottom-right. D2 3 upper exits top; 4 exits top-right corner; 3 lower exits bottom; 0 n/a.

Pattern of exits: D1: top-LEFT arm (5) → no exit; bottom-right (1) → exit. D3: 8 (top-leftish) → exits; 3 both → exits; 2 bottom-right → exits. D2: 4 top-right → exits; 3 both → exits. So D1's top-left arm is the ONLY case without an exit — and it's the ONLY case where a run sits on the border... or: the 5 run touches column 0? (16,0) is on the LEFT edge. Does touching the edge suppress extension? D3's 8 run touches nothing special; 2 touches nothing; 3 touches nothing. D2's runs touch nothing. Test input: 5 at (3,2), 4 at (4,0) ON THE EDGE!, 5 at (4,1), 2 at (5,0) EDGE!, 1 at (5,1), 1 at (6,2).

Hmm! D1: the 5-run includes (16,0) — a cell on the grid edge. Under "cells on edge can't extend"... in D2, 3's lower run end (13,10) is on the last row (edge) and still extended... no wait, extension FROM (13,10) downward is impossible anyway; the extension was above it. The endpoint (13,10) itself is on the edge but the ray came from above.

So maybe: extension happens from the endpoint that is NOT on/near the edge? D1 5-run: endpoints (15,1) [free] and (16,0) [edge]. Extension possible only from (15,1). NOT done. D1 1-run: endpoints (16,1) [adjacent to 5], (17,2) [free interior]. Extension from (17,2) done ✓. D3 8: endpoints (3,5)[free],[4,6][near 3 but interior]. Done ✓. 3-top: (3,8) free, (6,5) interior → done ✓. 2: (5,7) interior,(6,8) interior → done ✓. D2 4: endpoints (7,16),(8,15): both interior; extend from (7,16) up-right ✓.

Rule candidate: extend from the free endpoint; if BOTH endpoints free, pick ... D1 5: only one free endpoint → would extend ✗. STUPID. D1 kills everything.

NEW idea: maybe the extension fills to make the line REACH the CORNER or specific target cell: e.g., each ray extends until it reaches the grid boundary, but the STARTING run is selected... Or maybe rays extend until the painted segment length equals the distance pattern required to make all rays EQUAL LENGTH? D1 final rays: 1-ray len 7 added +2 = 9 cells. If 5-ray had been made equal... it'd be 9 too (full 15). Not equalizing.

Maybe lengths relate to object sizes: D1: 5 has 2 cells, got 0; 1 has 2, got 7. D3: 8: 2 cells, got 3; 3: 4, got 8; 2: 2, got 3. D2: 3: 4 cells, got 10; 4: 2, got 7; 0:1,n/a. No arithmetic relation obvious.

Try thinking of these as COLUMNS/LINES completion for a table? Like "fill in the missing cells of each diagonal to make the diagonal continuous across the entire grid whenever possible, EXCEPT when..." D1 5 anti-d=16: complete → needs (14,2)...(2,14): 14 cells. Not filled. 1 main d=15: complete → (18,3)..(24,9): 7 cells. FILLED. So completions happen only for some diagonals. What determines? Maybe diagonals whose COMPLETE version does not require crossing the bounding rectangle of the multi-colored region...? D1 5-complete crosses nowhere problematic.

Honestly, maybe think about it as: the colored cells form a path/polygon; the output draws the FULL perimeter of the convex hull projected onto diagonals? Convex hull of D1 cells: vertices (15,0),(17,2),(15,1)? hull edges: (15,0)-(17,2) is a diagonal! Slope: dr=2,dc=2 → main diagonal d=15 ✓ — the 1 line! And (17,2)-(15,1)? dr=-2,dc=-1 not diagonal. Hull corners: (15,0),(16,1)? (16,1) inside line segment (15,0)-(17,2)? (16,1): mid of (15,0),(17,2) ✓ yes. So hull edge = 1-line extended to connect (15,0)→(17,2). The 5 cells are INSIDE/ON hull. So rule: extend each colored line to connect the extreme points of the shape / make the outline continuous. The 5s lie inside the shape's hull, so they don't get extended (they're not "on the silhouette"). D3: 8 at (3,5),(4,6): hull of all cells (3,5),(3,8),(6,8),(6,5): edge (3,5)-(6,5)? dr=3,dc=0 vertical. Hmm hull edges: top (3,5)-(3,8), right (3,8)-(6,8)? dr=3,dc=0 vertical. 3-line (3,8),(6,5) anti-diag: that's a hull edge ✓ extended. 8-line (3,5),(4,6) main: is it a hull edge? Hull vertices: (3,5),(3,8),(6,8),(6,5): edges are the 3-line and the verticals and bottom (6,5)-(3,5). (4,6) is strictly inside. So 8-line is interior → should NOT extend ✗ but output extends 8!

Hmm. Unless hull computed differently... (4,6): is it inside triangle (3,5),(3,8),(6,5)? Point (4,6): barycentric? Lines: (3,5)-(6,5) is vertical x=5; (3,5)-(3,8) horizontal y=3; (3,8)-(6,5): c = 11-r, passes (4,7)? 11-4=7 ✓ and (4,6): 11-4=7 ≠ 6 → below the hypotenuse → outside! So (4,6) is outside the triangle → hull includes (4,6): hull vertices (3,5),(3,8),(6,8)? check (6,8) vs line (3,8)-(6,5): c=11-r=5 at r=6 → (6,5); (6,8) has c=8 > 5 → right of it. Hull: (3,5),(3,8),(6,8),(6,5) plus (4,6)? Edges: (3,5)-(3,8) top, (3,8)-(4,6)? dr=1,dc=-2 not diagonal.
